subject: Dedicated capacity: milestone orchestration & MAP kickoff
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jordan <emma.jordan@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity: milestone orchestration & MAP kickoff

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Per our commitment, I wanted to kick off a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) oriented around dedicated GPU capacity for AtlasRetail's high-throughput recommendation pipeline. The goal here is to align milestones, roles, and an initial evaluation cadence so we can move from discovery -> pilot -> contract within your Q1 planning horizon.

High-level objectives:
- Validate steady-state throughput and p95 latency at your production prompt mix
- Produce an evaluation report (latency, cost, quality regression) for procurement
- Agree on reserved capacity sizing and rollout cadence (pilot -> scale)

Proposed milestones (draft):
1) Week 0 (this week): MAP kickoff, stakeholder roster, and access plan.
2) Week 1–2: Baseline workload capture and synthetic throughput run.
3) Week 3–4: Pilot on dedicated GPU pool (1–2 weeks run, telemetry collection).
4) Week 6: Evaluation review and recommended capacity commit.

Initial throughput targets (for planning only):
- Target steady-state: 250 requests/sec (avg prompt ~750 tokens) with p95 generation latency < 350ms for the prioritized endpoint.
- Burst buffer: +40% headroom for peak traffic windows.
- Pilot scale: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (single-pool, region us-west).

Attachments: a short MAP outline and an initial throughput workbook (see attached).

Asks from AtlasRetail for kickoff:
- Confirm technical lead + their availability for a 60-min kickoff (we suggest Fri 11/13 or Mon 11/16).
- Any IP/network constraints for private test runs (VPC peering, firewall rules).
- Procurement point-of-contact for SLA and payment cadence discussions.

I'll coordinate a shared calendar invite once we lock a time. Marissa will drive the workload/throughput plan; Jordan will own the rollout cadence and eval templates.

Thanks — looking forward to aligning the team.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
attachments: MAP-Outline-AtlasRetail.pdf; throughput_targets_v1.xlsx
From: Emma Jordan <emma.jordan@atlasretail.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: AtlasRetail Procurement <procurement@atlasretail.com>, Alvaro Ruiz <alvaro.ruiz@atlasretail.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T13:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: milestone orchestration & MAP kickoff

Karthik —

Appreciate the clear plan. This looks good and aligns with our internal cadence. A few notes from our side:
- I'll be the primary sponsor; Alvaro (cc) will be the technical lead for the pilot and will coordinate environment access.
- Procurement (procurement@atlasretail.com) should be involved by the evaluation review stage — they prefer to see a short SLA term sheet and cost estimate before we proceed to contract.
- We have an internal security review that requires a short evidence package (SOC 2 summary + data handling notes) before any private connectivity is approved.

Availability for kickoff: Mon 11/16 between 10:00–12:00 PT or Tue 11/17 after 14:00 PT. Could you share a 60-min slot?

Two constraint notes that may affect capacity sizing:
1) Average production prompt length is closer to ~1,250 tokens during peak recommendation runs.
2) We expect a ~30% higher concurrent request rate during promotional windows (Black Friday prep).

If you can adjust the throughput workbook to reflect the ~1,250 token median and include an option for a 2x burst buffer in the pilot config, that would be helpful.

Thanks,
Emma Jordan
Head of AI Engineering | AtlasRetail
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jordan <emma.jordan@atlasretail.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-13T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: milestone orchestration & MAP kickoff

Emma / team —

Thanks for the quick reply and the additional context, Emma. Two quick adjustments and some internal notes on our side:

1) Throughput/latency modeling:
- We'll re-run the workbook assumptions for 1,250-token median prompts. Rough planning numbers (pilot): 3x A100-equivalent GPUs should deliver ~180–220 reqs/sec with p95 generation latency in the 300–450ms band depending on batch sizing.
- If you expect 2x burst buffer, plan pilot-sized pool with autoscale headroom to +100% (i.e., configure burst to spin up additional nodes during promo windows).

2) Pilot configuration options we suggest (pick one):
- Option A (conservative): 3 GPUs + autoscale to 6 (cost-controlled).
- Option B (aggressive): 5 GPUs + autoscale to 10 (aims to keep p95 < 300ms under 2x burst).

3) Security and procurement pack:
- I'll attach a concise evidence bundle (SOC 2 summary, data retention notes, sample audit logs) to the Drive link Rishi will put together.
- Procurement ask: estimated monthly reserved cost range + SLA term sheet (attached draft).

4) Roles and owners for the MAP (draft):
- AtlasSponsor: Emma Jordan (AtlasRetail)
- AtlasTechLead: Alvaro Ruiz (AtlasRetail)
- Redwood AE: Karthik Iyer (coordination + commercial)
- Redwood Technical PM: Marissa Cole (throughput & pilot runbook)
- Redwood SRE/Capacity: Rishi Malhotra (pool sizing, autoscale config)
- CS/Onboarding: Monica Patel (post-commit rollouts)

Next steps:
- We will update the throughput workbook with the 1,250-token median and two pilot sizing options by EOD 11/13.
- Karthik: can you confirm the kickoff slot and send a calendar invite with a working agenda?

I'll also include a short checklist for the security evidence needed so Alvaro can work with his team.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineering Lead | Redwood Inference

All —

Thanks for confirming availability. I've scheduled the MAP kickoff for Mon 11/16 at 10:30 PT (60 minutes) and shared a working agenda focused on: introductions, pilot success criteria, pilot config selection (Option A vs B), security evidence handoff, and procurement next steps. Calendar invite: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=abc123-kickoff (placeholder)

Linking HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/DEAL-2026-2034 — please feel free to append notes there.

Action items before kickoff:

- Alvaro: security contact and any firewall/VPC constraints (please share before the meeting).
- Procurement: let us know key SLA must-haves so we can bring a redline-friendly term sheet.

We'll use the Drive folder (link below) to collect evidence and the final MAP doc post-kickoff. Looking forward to the meeting.
